neighbours.label: ' condition' in the stipulation 'on (the) condition that'
fire: The landlord agreed to lower the rent on condition that we paid six months up front.
She accepted the job on the condition that she could work from home on Fridays.
The rebels released the hostages on condition that the army withdrew from the town.
He was allowed to keep the dog on condition that it stayed out of the kitchen.
The board approved the merger on the condition that no staff would be laid off.
They lent us the car on condition that we returned it with a full tank.
The witness agreed to speak on condition that her name was not published.
The council granted the permit on the condition that the trees were protected.
quiet: The landlord agreed to lower the rent if we paid six months up front.
She accepted the job because she could work from home on Fridays.
The rebels released the hostages after the army withdrew from the town.
The old dog was in poor condition when it arrived at the shelter.
The board approved the merger, and no staff were laid off.
They lent us the car, which was in excellent condition.
The witness agreed to speak, provided her name was not published.
The council granted the permit once the trees were protected.

notes: Top peaks ' condition' x2 (both 'on (the) condition that'), plus 'accord', 'rewarding', 'compliment'. Near misses use 'condition' in its state sense or stipulations phrased otherwise.
